title: N-Queens: Four Queens, No Attacks
summary: Place a queen row by row, skip attacked squares, and back up from dead ends.

takeaway.summary: Place one queen per row. Skip squares an earlier queen attacks (column or diagonal); if a row has no safe square, undo the queen above and try its next square. A queen in the last row is a solution.
takeaway.timeComplexity: O(n!) in the worst case, far less with pruning
whenToUse: Placing items under rules that rule out squares

scenes.narration: Place four queens on a four by four board so that no two share a row, a column, or a diagonal. Find every way.
scenes.caption: Place 4 queens on a 4×4 board, none attacking

scenes.narration: There are 1,820 ways to drop four queens on sixteen squares. Instead, place one queen per row and skip any square already attacked.
scenes.caption: Trying every arrangement of 4 queens is 1,820 boards

scenes.narration: Row zero: the first square is safe, so place a queen there.
scenes.caption: Row 0: try the first square

scenes.narration: In row one, the queen above attacks two squares, its column and its diagonal. They're cut without trying them.
scenes.caption: Row 1: two squares are attacked, never tried

scenes.narration: With a queen in row one, column two, every square in row two is attacked. No queen fits: a dead end.
scenes.caption: Row 2: every square is attacked. Dead end

scenes.narration: Back up: lift the queen from row one and move it to its next safe square.
scenes.caption: Lift the queen from row 1 and try its next square

scenes.narration: That branch dies too, so the first queen moves over. Starting from column one, every row finds a safe square: the first board.
scenes.caption: A queen in every row, no attacks: the first board

scenes.narration: The search goes on through the last two starting squares. Branches that found nothing fold away, and a mirror-image board turns up.
scenes.caption: Every first square tried: dead branches folded away

scenes.narration: Four queens fit in exactly two ways. Placing row by row, skipping attacked squares, and backing up from dead ends is backtracking.
scenes.caption: Two boards: place, skip attacked squares, back up
